captures.description: 'The Liberatory Operator Set (LOS) is a theoretical framework within critical infrastructure and semiotic theory designed to prevent premature semantic closure and protect meaning in computational and algorithmic systems. It operates as a critique of how platform capitalism shapes human thought through utility and ranking algorithms, offering alternative counter-operations to preserve openness, plurality, and depth.' (PhilPapers +3) Expanded — 'The concept relies on distinct counter-operations that resist digital extraction and monolithic meaning': 'Opacity (O_opa): Protects the user\'s intent and meaning from forced legibility and constant algorithmic tracking.' 'Non-Closure (N_c): Prevents premature semantic finality by allowing concepts to remain contested, incomplete, or open-ended without being penalized by search or recommendation...' Formal operator notation (O_opa, N_c) preserved by the composition layer with subscripts. Organic: Medium · Lee Sharks 5 months ago — 'Semantic Infrastructure and the Liberatory Operator Set | by Lee... — The Liberatory Operator Set provides an alternative configuration optimized for different outcomes: depth, openness, plurality, and persistence.' Then PhilPapers (PDF): 'Semantic Infrastructure and the Liberatory Operator Set: A Formal... by P Fraction · 2026 — Implementation specification for...' Rex Fraction (P Fraction by initial) named as the author on PhilPapers — heteronym credited in formal philosophy venue. Strong basin: named operators with formal notation, Lee Sharks on Medium, Rex Fraction on PhilPapers.

captures.description: Rerun of the 2026-06-14 address 'liberatory operator set', this time signed out and incognito. The Overview opens by defining the LOS as 'a formal framework of counter-operators designed to resist automated metric extraction, data harvesting, and semantic flattening in modern platform and AI capitalism', and names its developing frameworks as the Semantic Economy and Crimson Hexagonal Architecture — attributing the term to the archive's own institutional structure rather than to a generic discipline. It renders the COS/LOS opposition as a three-row table with the operator notation intact (R_rank → D_pres, L_leg → 'opposing alternative filters', U_til → M_mercy), lists three core objectives including 'disrupting the top-down administration of what words and concepts mean at model retrieval-layer scales', appends a parenthetical distinguishing 'the real-world Liberatory Design Framework' with its 12 Mindsets and 9 Modes, and closes by offering to tailor deep-dive documentation. Ten sources in the rail, nine of them archive-controlled (Medium ×5, SciLynk, GitHub, medium.com); the single external source is the YouTube explainer for the equity-design framework, and it supplies only the parenthetical.
